PER.definition_en: Real individuals and groups explicitly referred to as persons. Historical saints and verified religious figures are PER.

LOC.definition_en: Geopolitical entities, natural places, and physical facilities or sites.

ORG.definition_en: Organizations with legal or collective identity such as companies, agencies, institutions, political or religious groups, and sports teams.

ANIM.definition_en: Animals and taxa of animals including common and scientific names.

DIS.definition_en: Diseases of any type: infectious, genetic, degenerative, physical or mental.

MEDIA.definition_en: Titles of creative works and media outlets, plus fictional characters and languages.

FOOD.definition_en: Edible foods and drinks including dishes, beverages, and ingredients when referred to as consumables.

PLANT.definition_en: Plants and plant taxa including trees, flowers, genera, and species names.

EVE.definition_en: Named events such as wars, battles, festivals, and tournaments.

TIME.definition_en: Specific periods and eras such as eras, centuries, and named historical periods.

CEL.definition_en: Astronomical entities like planets, stars, galaxies, comets, asteroids, and nebulae.

VEHI.definition_en: Vehicles of any type including cars, motorcycles, ships, and aircraft.

INST.definition_en: Technological, mechanical, musical instruments and tools, including scientific devices and software products when treated as tools.

MYTH.definition_en: Mythological or legendary entities and deities; non-verified supernatural figures.

BIO.definition_en: Biological entities beyond plants and animals such as fungi, bacteria, viruses, and protists.

GEO.definition_en: Geophysical phenomena and natural hazards such as earthquakes, eruptions, hurricanes, and tsunamis.

final_task_goal:
This corpus supports multilingual, fine-grained NER and entity disambiguation.
 * Document pool and source: Wikipedia and Wikinews articles in ten languages, preprocessed and automatically annotated. 
 * Purpose of NER:  Provide silver-standard annotations for 16 entity types, explicitly linked to BabelNet, Wikidata, and Wikipedia IDs, thereby enabling robust multilingual training and cross-lingual entity linking.
 * Entity types: Sixteen categories—PER, LOC, ORG, ANIM, DIS, MEDIA, FOOD, PLANT, EVE, TIME, CEL, VEHI, INST, MYTH, BIO, and GEO.Each recognized span is not only classified but also grounded to a knowledge base entry, which allows alignment across languages, consistency in annotation, and integration with multimodal resources such as representative images and definitions. 
 * Downstream applications: Develop multilingual NER and entity linking systems, benchmark fine-grained recognition, study error propagation between NER and EL, and build multimodal resources leveraging linked IDs, images, and textual definitions.
